I am 60 this year. I have farmed this 2 mu of land for 40 years. My mother taught me, and I watched my neighbors. I never went to school, but I know this land.

For winter wheat, I sow right after National Day in October. I buy improved seeds from the shop in town — the kind everyone plants, not the old ones we kept at home. Before sowing, I spread half a 50‑kg bag of compound fertilizer on each mu. That is 25 kg per mu. Then in spring, when the wheat turns green around Qingming, I spread 20 kg of urea per mu. I buy urea in 40‑kg bags, so one bag is enough for my 2 mu. I irrigate three times: once before winter so the wheat does not freeze, once at Qingming when it shoots up fast, and once when the ears come out. I spray pesticide twice — once in spring when the aphids come, and once if I see rust on the leaves. I rotary till before planting. Last year I got about 900 jin per mu, and if the weather is good this year I expect the same.

For summer maize, as soon as the wheat is cut in early June, I plant maize. I buy hybrid seeds in the red packets — Li from the east side of the village had good luck with those last year, so I bought the same. I put down half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and when the maize is knee‑high I spread 20 kg of urea per mu. I irrigate twice if the rain does not come — once when the seedlings are small, and once when the tassels come out. I spray twice if the armyworms show up. I rotary till after wheat harvest. I expect about 1,000 jin per mu.

I have seven people in my house. Some work in the city and send money back, but fertilizer is still expensive. I would rather put a little more fertilizer than risk losing yield — a bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. So I do what I did last year, and I watch my neighbors. If they use the same amount, I use the same amount. Change is dangerous.
